```{r}
data <- updated_analysis_three_domain

head(data)
```

```{r}
model1 <- lm(P_C_DayD ~ high_ability * sub_under, data = data)
summary(model1)
```
```{r}
# Load required library
library(ggplot2)

# Create an interaction plot
ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(high_ability), y = P_C_DayD, color = factor(sub_under))) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", aes(group = factor(sub_under))) +
  labs(title = "Interaction between High Ability and Objective Underachievement",
       x = "High Ability Status",
       y = "P_C_DayD",
       color = "Subjective Underachievement") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("blue", "red"),
                    labels = c("No", "Yes")) +
  theme_minimal()
```
If you are not high-ability student, the subjective underachieving do not have effect on the relationship between high ability and positive constructive daydreaming. However, if students are identified as high-ability, people who are not subjective underachieving tend to have greater daydreaming, compare those who are.
